resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says circa 1919. The 1919-20 report says the tower had been in service since July 15, and a 1923 item says it was erected in 1920. The record uses 1919 (circa), and the story gives both years.
The register says 47 feet, the 1919-20 report says 45 feet, and the 1923 item says fifty feet. The record keeps 13.7 m (45 ft), as in the brief, and the story reports all three.
The register gives 1,368 ft (417 m); the 1923 item gives about 1,400 feet above sea level. The record uses the register figure.

notes_for_editor: The Greystone link is solid across the register, the NHLR and Wikipedia. The build year (circa 1919 versus 1920) and the height (45, 47 or fifty feet) differ across sources; the brief's 13.7 m follows the 45-foot figure. The 'Foundation' photo on the register is undated and has no image URL captured, so no photos entry is recorded. Access to the original site is not described in any source I read; the 119firecontrol.com page had no Edison or Greystone match and the NJ DEP fire-towers page returned no readable text. The brief's record has no errors I could confirm.
